Abstract:
This paper presents a rigorous design and evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline for fine-tuning foundation models implemented in PyTorch, integrated with multi-layer safety guardrails. We introduce a synchronized methodological framework that combines approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and prompt composition with LoRA-adapted fine-tuning, while enforcing guardrails for toxicity, personally identifiable information (PII), and jailbreak attempts. Using controlled experiments on open-domain QA and safety stress tests, we quantify accuracy–latency trade-offs and demonstrate significant reductions in safety violations with minimal impact on utility. We contribute: (i) a formal conceptual model linking data quality, retrieval recall, prompt coherence, and safety constraints to response quality; (ii) a reproducible PyTorch training and evaluation protocol; and (iii) regulator-aware recommendations aligning with responsible AI guidelines.
